answer: Each agent identity must maintain a bonded stake that is locked before it can submit bids, and disputes trigger a challenge window in which other agents can present signed evidence of duplicated control, such as matching payment keys or synchronized task responses. A successful challenge slashes the bond and splits the proceeds with the challenger. Spinning up a swarm therefore requires separate capital for every identity, and detected clones lose it; the attacker cannot get cheap, disposable votes for a voyage, even when offering nectar or jade as bait.
